title.narrative: Effective Economic Policies and Access to Finance

description.narrative: The theory of change is premised on the fact that most of the Commonwealth's small and vulnerable states are faced with structural economic constraints, climate and disaster vulnerability, high debt burdens and limited fiscal space, ineligibility for concessional finance largely due to income-based criteria, and Weak domestic revenue bases. If these countries can then be supported with advocacy efforts that bear concrete outcomes for fairer access to long-term and concessional finance as well being supported with adoption and implementation of effective fiscal and domestic resource mobilisation policies, they will achieve resilient economies and sustainable prosperity. This project, therefore, aims at helping the small and vulnerable states gain access to affordable and sustainable finance. This will be achieved primarily through Advocacy and technical assistance around fiscal sustainability. This advocacy will be grounded not only in influencing the fairness of the global financing frameworks but also in strengthening the capacity of small states to effectively access and absorb these resources. This will entail supporting them with robust and coherent economic policies, enhanced institutional and technical implementation capacities, and the ability to leverage existing domestic and regional resources. Central to this approach will be strengthening domestic resource mobilisation to ensure long-term financial sustainability and reduce overreliance on external funding. Knowledge generation will play a critical role of assessing what the advocacy efforts have achieved to date and identifying the remaining gaps in financial instruments, including whether they sufficiently account for the multidimensional vulnerabilities of small states. Targeted technical assistance will be provided based on identified gaps, building on strategic partnerships in areas beyond the Commonwealth Secretariat’s direct capacity. For the project's expected outcomes and impacts, see the Indicators Section.
